groups.text: It is currently 19 degrees and partly cloudy in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

Anthropic is now embedding invisible watermarks in all text generated by Claude globally. This move follows the company signing the EU AI Act Code of Practice on transparency for AI-generated content. Starting in August 2026, new models will ship with these machine-readable labels built in from day one. The policy extends across all products, including the API and Claude Code, while files like images will receive signed provenance metadata following the C2PA standard. Anthropic notes that these watermarks may persist through some editing, though heavy changes or format shifts can strip them entirely. Because users often use AI to translate or edit their own writing, a watermark does not definitively prove Claude wrote the content. To support this system, the company plans to release verification tools for third-party use. Existing models will undergo a transition period as Anthropic works to retrofit them with these labels.

Three of FIFA's six confederations have issued an open letter to the football family, accusing President Gianni Infantino of a fundamental breach of trust. UEFA, CONCACAF, and AFC are attacking his conduct regarding the proposed sale of a stake in World Cup commercial rights, calling for leadership that actually works for the game. In other sports news, Paris is currently hosting the third Esports World Cup. Thousands of competitors have gathered in the city to vie for 25 titles across 24 different esports. Shifting to the legal system in the United States, a trial has begun in Las Vegas for a former gang leader accused of orchestrating the murder of rapper Tupac Shakur. The proceedings are expected to last nearly a month, coming thirty years after the death of the California artist remained an unsolved mystery.

Colombia has declared a national emergency following a magnitude 7.4 earthquake, the strongest the country has seen in a decade. The quake struck Monday morning near San José del Palmar in the Chocó region along the Pacific coast, triggering nearly 50 aftershocks. Local media report more than 130 deaths and hundreds of injuries, while approximately 2,000 people remain missing. President Abelardo de la Espriella says thousands of homes were damaged or destroyed. Rescue workers are currently searching for survivors in the ruins of collapsed buildings in Cali and Manizales, where a tower of the city's cathedral was damaged. Heavy casualties are also reported in Pereira, located in the coffee-growing region of Risaralda. Witnesses describe scenes of panic, with residents fleeing into the streets or jumping from windows as the ground shook.

OpenAI has launched a new AI model called GPT-5.6-Cyber, specifically designed for authorized cybersecurity work. The company says this model is better at finding zero-days and creating exploit chains than its predecessor, GPT-5.6-Sol, which often refused risky dual-use prompts. In testing, the new model achieved a 95 percent completion rate for tasks like authentication bypass and privilege escalation. OpenAI reports that the tool has already discovered security flaws in an unnamed mobile operating system and a high-severity vulnerability in Chrome's V8 JavaScript engine. Alongside this release, OpenAI is expanding its Daybreak Cyber Partner program to give more organizations access to the technology. In separate news from Europe, Poland has begun the launch process for the ORP Wicher. This is the first of three new-generation frigates being built under the 3.5 billion dollar Miecznik programme to modernize the Polish navy and protect maritime infrastructure.

CMB.TECH is capitalizing on high crude carrier values by selling the Bristol, a two-year-old suezmax tanker built in 2024. The Alexander Saverys-led Belgian group expects to lock in a capital gain of about 56.9 million dollars from the sale, which will be recorded in the fourth quarter. This transaction brings CMB.TECH's total gains from tanker sales in 2026 to around 620 million dollars, funds the company intends to use for debt repayment and shareholder distributions. In a different sector of the maritime market, Star Bulk Carriers has walked away from a 470.5 million dollar agreement to acquire 16 bulkers from Diana Shipping. The two Greek owners mutually terminated the deal at Star Bulk's request due to a lack of progress in Diana's attempt to take over Genco Shipping and Trading. While Star Bulk exits the deal, Diana maintains its cash-and-stock offer for Genco despite a previous loss in a June proxy fight.

The UK Competition and Markets Authority is investigating a completed acquisition in the distribution and service industries. The regulator has launched an inquiry into NRG Fleet Services following its purchase of Specialist Fleet Services. To maintain the status quo during this review, the CMA served an initial enforcement order on August 10 under the Enterprise Act 2002. This legal move prevents the companies from fully integrating while the agency determines if the merger harms competition. The case is currently open and moving toward a phase one investigation. The regulator is now seeking written representations regarding any potential competition issues from outside parties.

Biologist Grace Carroll suggests that the relationship between humans and cats may be undergoing a transformation beyond the domestication that occurred thousands of years ago. Research on red foxes in London and deer in Dublin shows that animals more willing to tolerate or seek out humans often gain advantages in urban environments. This raises the possibility that cats are still evolving to become more docile as they live alongside people, though some argue the change is actually social, with humans now treating cats as family members. In a different vein of companionship, the historical friendship between Isaac Newton and Edmond Halley demonstrates how personal bonds can transform human knowledge. Their connection began in August 1684 when Halley traveled from London to Cambridge to ask Newton about planetary trajectories. This partnership highlights that scientific breakthroughs often rely on more than just individual genius.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be partly cloudy with temperatures between 19 and 24 degrees and no rain expected.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.
On your calendar today: personal calendar: all day: Sommerferien 2026 Berlin, at 14:00, NAS Sync, at 15:00, RAYX Meeting, and at 18:00, Krebs at c-base.
Mail worth checking: Discord sent urgent alerts regarding an email change and a scheduled account deletion. You also have a sale notification from Steam.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
